fanOuts.intro: Each published rule version is decided for every business of its level, a batch at a time, behind the global hold. Every regulatory role reads the runs; an admin holds, pauses, resumes, cancels and rolls back.
fanOuts.meaning.running: Deciding the version for each business of its level, a batch of 1,000 at a time.
fanOuts.meaning.held: Stopped at a batch boundary by the global hold; it carries on by itself once the hold is released.
fanOuts.meaning.paused: Stopped at a batch boundary by a person, or by the run itself when too many results flipped; it runs again only when an admin resumes it.
fanOuts.meaning.completed: Every business of the level was decided.
fanOuts.meaning.cancelled: Stopped for good; the decisions it made stay.
fanOuts.meaning.disabled: Published while fan-outs were switched off, so it never ran; each business is decided when its profile next changes.
fanOuts.meaning.failed: A batch kept failing after its retries. The decisions made before it stay.

fanOut.control.cancelDescription: The run stops at its next batch boundary for good. The decisions it made stay; to take them back, roll the version back. The engine keeps your reason in its audit log.

workbench.claimedBy: Claimed by {who} on {when}: they decide it, or a reviewer returns it to the queue
workbench.claimed: The task is yours: draft or edit it, then decide.
workbench.error.task: This is not a review task's id.
workbench.edit.cited: Citations added: {count}; the rulebook found every quote in its clause.
workbench.edit.meanwhileNothingSaved: Nothing was saved. The form now shows the draft as the rulebook holds it: make your change again if it still applies.
workbench.decide.approved: Approved: the round is complete and the version is approved.
workbench.decide.returned: Returned to draft: the rework has a new task.
workbench.decide.approvalRecorded: Your approval is recorded: {count} of {required} approvals.
workbench.decide.needsAnother: A second, different reviewer completes the round.
workbench.publishLink: Publish it from the version's page
workbench.introSeed: A draft the seed calendar wrote, to check against the instrument it cites: claim the task to edit the draft, then a reviewer approves it, or it is returned or rejected.
workbench.introCandidate: A rule candidate the pipeline extracted from a document: claim the task to draft a version from it and edit that draft, then a reviewer approves it, or it is returned or rejected.
workbench.ontologyMissing: The ontology could not be read, so the conditions show their values as stored, without labels or meanings, and the editor suggests no attribute.
workbench.source.heading: Source
workbench.source.none: The draft cites no document yet. Citations added to the draft show their documents here.
workbench.source.noFile: The pipeline stores no file for this document: it reached the rulebook another way.
workbench.source.fileUnread: Whether the pipeline stores a file for it could not be read.
workbench.source.noClauses: The rulebook holds no clause of this document.
workbench.source.unmatched: A quote did not match this clause word for word, so the whole clause is marked:
workbench.source.noCitations: The draft cites no clause yet.
workbench.candidate.heading: Candidate
workbench.candidate.unparseableBody: The model's answer could not be read as a candidate, twice. Draft the rule by hand: the draft form starts empty.
workbench.candidate.keyKnown: A rule has this key: the draft becomes its next version.
workbench.candidate.keyUnknown: No rule has this key yet: drafting into it starts a new rule.
workbench.candidate.problems: What does not map, as the rulebook found it
workbench.rule.heading: Rule
workbench.rule.noDraft: No version is drafted from the candidate yet.
workbench.rule.accessDetail: The draft is shown, and nothing is sent to the rulebook from here.
workbench.draftView.templateUnread: The obligation could not be read.
workbench.claim.otherTail: Only they draft and edit it; a reviewer may still decide it.
workbench.field.title: Title
workbench.field.effectiveToHelp: The day the version stops being in force, not included. Leave it empty for an open-ended version.
workbench.field.oneOff: A duty that does not recur falls due a number of days after it applies, set below.
workbench.field.dueMonthOffset: Months after the month that follows the period
workbench.field.dueMonthOffsetHelp: 0 is the month that follows the period; at most {max}.
workbench.field.templateTitle: What the business has to do
workbench.field.dueInDaysHelp: For a duty that does not recur: days after it applies. Leave it empty for a recurring duty.
workbench.field.todoHelp: One per line, at most {max}: what an analyst answers before publication.
workbench.citations.addHelp: Pick a clause of a document the draft rests on, then type or paste the words of it the rule rests on. The rulebook verifies every quote and stores all of them or none.
workbench.citations.ownHelp: Pick a clause of the candidate's document, then type or paste the words of it the rule rests on. Leaving no row cites nothing for now.
workbench.citations.noClauses: No clause can be cited: the documents' clauses could not be read.
workbench.citations.quoteHelp: The clause's words, at most {max} characters.
workbench.citations.found: The clause holds this quote word for word.
workbench.citations.notFound: The clause does not hold this quote word for word. The rulebook verifies by a match score, so small differences may still pass.
workbench.edit.heading: Edit the draft
workbench.edit.unavailable: The draft cannot be edited here.
workbench.edit.noteHelp: Optional, at most {max} characters. The decision audit keeps it with the edit.
workbench.draft.heading: Draft a version from the candidate
workbench.draft.unavailable: No version can be drafted here.
workbench.draft.intro: The version starts from what the candidate proposes, with your changes. The rulebook checks it as it checks the seed calendar and lists every problem; nothing is stored until it passes.
workbench.draft.ruleKeyHelp: A rule's key, such as example_rule: the version becomes the rule's next one.
workbench.draft.ruleKeyKnown: A rule has this key: the version becomes its next one.
workbench.draft.ruleKeyNew: No rule may have this key yet: the version is the first of a new rule.
workbench.draft.newRule: Start a new rule with this key
workbench.draft.citeOwn: Cite quotes of my own instead
workbench.draft.relationsLegend: Relations of the document to take on
workbench.draft.noRelations: The document has no open relation candidate.
workbench.draft.relationTargetRequired: This kind of relation needs the version it points at.
workbench.draft.relationTargetOptional: Optional: without one, the relation points at the aligned entity.
workbench.decide.heading: Decide
workbench.decide.closed: The task is decided: nothing more is decided here.
workbench.decide.approveIntro: Approving submits the draft and approves it. One approval completes a round; a high-impact version needs two different reviewers. Approving never publishes: the version is published from its own page.
workbench.decide.highImpactHelp: Tagged before this approval counts, so a second, different reviewer must approve too.
workbench.decide.highImpactSet: The version is high impact: a second, different reviewer must approve. The tag stays once set.
workbench.decide.noteHelp: At most {max} characters, kept with the decision.
workbench.decide.approveConfirm: The rulebook records your approval with your user id and the note. The version is approved when the round has the approvals it needs.
workbench.decide.approveConfirmHigh: The rulebook tags the version high impact, then records your approval with your user id and the note. A second, different reviewer must approve before the version is approved.
workbench.decide.returnHelp: Say what needs rework. The version goes back to draft and a new task opens for it.
workbench.decide.returnConfirm: The rulebook returns the version to draft, closes this task with your note and opens a new task for the rework. The round's approvals no longer count.
workbench.decide.rejectIntro: Rejecting closes the task with your note and leaves the version a draft.
workbench.decide.rejectCandidateIntro: Rejecting closes the task and rejects the candidate with your reason and note. A draft made from it is closed for good and its relation candidates open again.
workbench.decide.rejectHelp: Say why. The rulebook keeps the note with the decision.
workbench.decide.rejectConfirm: The rulebook closes this task with your note. The version stays a draft.
workbench.decide.rejectCandidateConfirm: The rulebook closes this task and rejects the candidate with your reason and note. A draft made from it is closed for good.
workbench.approvals.another: A second, different reviewer completes it.
workbench.diff.heading: What changed
workbench.diff.notDrafted: Nothing to compare until a version is drafted.
workbench.diff.noPrevious: The rule has no earlier version to compare with.
workbench.history.heading: History
workbench.history.noAudit: The version has no decision recorded yet.
rules.intro: Every rule the rulebook holds, by key, with its regulator and the title of its latest version. A rule arrives with its first version; its versions move through review on the rule version pages.
rules.emptyTitle: The rulebook holds no rule yet
rules.emptyBody: A rule arrives with its first version: the seed command writes the calendar's drafts, and the review workbench drafts one from a rule candidate.
rules.filterHelp: Every word must appear in the rule key, the title or the regulator.
rules.noMatch: No rule matches every word typed.
rules.caption: {count} rules by key.
rules.column.title: Title of the latest version
llm.editBody: This page reads the gateway and changes nothing. A prompt or a route changes with a release of the gateway; changing one here waits for:
llm.prompts.intro: The prompts the LLM gateway serves, each by name and version, with its owner, the eval cases that guard it and the hash of its text.
llm.prompts.emptyBody: Its prompt registry is empty. Prompts arrive with a release of the gateway.
llm.prompts.caption: {count} prompts by name and version.
llm.models.intro: The model route of each feature, as the gateway applies it: the primary model and its fallback, the providers it may use, the sort, the reasoning effort and the time limit.
llm.models.emptyBody: Its routing table is empty, so no feature can call a model.
llm.models.caption: {count} features with their routes.
llm.usage.intro: Spend against the gateway's monthly budgets: one for each tenant and one for each feature. Every feature's budget for the month shows first; ask for a tenant's or a feature's.
llm.usage.tenantHelp: Optional: a tenant's budget. A feature then narrows its spend.
llm.usage.tenantInvalid: This is not a tenant id (a UUID).
llm.usage.featureInvalid: Choose a feature from the list.
llm.usage.monthHelp: YYYY-MM, in UTC as the gateway counts months.
llm.usage.monthInvalid: Give the month as YYYY-MM, such as 2000-01.
llm.usage.budgetsNote: The budgets are the gateway's settings; this page reads them and changes nothing. Spend is shown to every place the ledger keeps.
llm.usage.narrowedNote: The spend is {feature}'s alone; the budget is the tenant's for every feature, so the share and the alarm compare the two. Ask without a feature for the tenant's whole spend.
profileReview.intro: One profile node of one tenant: its open review tasks, and what the applicability engine evaluates for it in a financial year. The profile service acts for the tenant the lookup names.
profileReview.tenantInvalid: This is not a tenant id (a UUID).
profileReview.nodeInvalid: This is not a node id (a UUID): a business, a registration or a location.
profileReview.help: Give a tenant's id and the id of one of its nodes: a business (its legal entity), a registration or a location. The profile service answers only for the tenant named.
profileReview.notFoundTitle: No node with this id in this tenant
profileReview.notFoundBody: The profile service holds no node with this id for the tenant named. Check both ids: a node belongs to one tenant.
profileReview.fact.name: Name
profileReview.noParent: None: a legal entity is the top of its business
profileReview.ontologyMissing: The ontology could not be read, so attributes and values are shown as stored.
profileReview.noTasksTitle: No review task is open on this node
profileReview.noTasksBody: A task opens when the profile service cannot settle a value by itself: a registration no lookup knows, an answer that does not apply, a year to confirm.
profileReview.tasksRegion: Table of the node's review tasks
profileReview.closingNote: This page reads only. A task closes when the attribute is answered on the business's own pages; no route closes one from here.
profileReview.snapshotFacts: Profile version {version}, with values inherited from {ancestors} ancestors.
profileReview.noValuesTitle: No value is held for this node
profileReview.noValuesBody: Neither this node nor its ancestors hold a value for {fy} yet.
profileReview.reason.notApplicable: The business answered that it does not apply
profileReview.reason.confirmFinancialYea: A value to confirm for a new financial year
profileReview.reason.verifyRegistration: No lookup could verify the registration
system.intro: Every service behind the web app, as this web server reaches it: whether it answers its health check and is ready to serve, and what the screen registry says about it. Each probe waits at most {seconds} seconds.
system.someDown: Services that do not answer their health check: {count}
system.someDownBody: Their rows say why: the address could not be reached, no answer came within the time limit, or the service answered with an error. The screens that call them show the failure with its correlation id.
system.servicesCaption: {count} services in the order the stack starts them.
system.registryIntro: From the screen registry: the built screens each service serves, and the routes screens still wait for from it, with who delivers them. A service that is down takes those screens with it.
system.registryCaption: Each service's screens and awaited routes.
system.fact.timeout: Time limit of a service call
system.fact.telemetry: OpenTelemetry, as it registered when this server started
system.telemetryLocal: On, with no exporter configured: spans stay in this server
system.telemetryExporting: On, exporting over OTLP, with every query and personal value taken out of the spans
system.telemetryFailed: Off: registration failed at startup (telemetry_registration_failed in the server's log)
system.telemetryUnknown: Not known: no registration was recorded in this server process
pipelineWrites.adminRequired: Only an admin changes the pipeline
pipelineWrites.adminRequiredDetail: Analysts and reviewers read the sources and the pipeline; an admin edits a source, fetches one, uploads a document, retries a document, requeues an outbox row and resolves or dismisses a task.
pipelineWrites.tokenMissing: The write token is not configured
pipelineWrites.tokenMissingDetail: Set CW_WEB_RULEBOOK_WRITE_TOKEN to the shared write token the pipeline reads as its CW_RULEBOOK_WRITE_TOKEN.
pipelineWrites.tokenInvalid: The pipeline refused the write token
pipelineWrites.tokenInvalidDetail: The pipeline rejected CW_WEB_RULEBOOK_WRITE_TOKEN. Check that it matches the pipeline's CW_RULEBOOK_WRITE_TOKEN.
pipelineWrites.writesDisabledDetail: The pipeline has no CW_RULEBOOK_WRITE_TOKEN set, so it refuses every write. Set it on the pipeline, and set CW_WEB_RULEBOOK_WRITE_TOKEN here to the same value.
rawDocument.notFound: No stored document has this id
rawDocument.notFoundDetail: Check the id: the pipeline holds no stored document under it, or the address is not one of its documents.
rawDocument.forbidden: The pipeline refused to serve the file
rawDocument.forbiddenDetail: The stored files are the regulatory team's: analysts, reviewers and admins read them.
rawDocument.unreadable: The stored file cannot be served
rawDocument.unreadableDetail: The raw store has no file under the document's key, or its bytes no longer match the digest the record names, so nothing is served in its place.
rawDocument.storeUnavailable: The raw store did not answer
rawDocument.storeUnavailableDetail: The pipeline could not read its raw store. Open the file again in a moment.
handlers.crossOrigin: Refused: the request came from another site
handlers.crossOriginDetail: This is taken only from this site's own pages.
handlers.signInDetail: Your session has ended. Sign in, open the page again and try once more.
handlers.roleRequiredDetail: It is for these roles only: {roles}.
upload.error.noSourceDetail: The pipeline holds no source under this key. Open the source from the list of sources and upload from its page.
upload.error.notMultipart: The upload is not a form with a file
upload.error.notMultipartDetail: Send the upload form from the source's page: the file and its fields as multipart/form-data.
upload.error.tooLarge: The file is larger than the pipeline takes
upload.error.tooLargeDetail: The pipeline takes a file of at most {limit}, with its fields. Nothing was stored.
upload.error.tooLargePipeline: The pipeline refused it under its own limit, which is lower than this server's. Nothing was stored.
upload.error.tooLargePipelineDetail: The pipeline refused it under its own limit: {detail}. Nothing was stored.
upload.error.malformed: The upload could not be read
upload.error.malformedDetail: The form's fields come first and the file last, and the body must end where the form ends. Nothing was stored: send the form again from the source's page.
upload.error.unsupported: Only a PDF or an HTML page can be uploaded
upload.error.unsupportedDetail: The file was sent as {type}. Upload a PDF or an HTML page; nothing was stored.
upload.error.unsupportedNone: The file was sent without a type. Upload a PDF or an HTML page; nothing was stored.
upload.error.reasonShort: Say why in at least {min} characters.
upload.error.date: Give the publication date as a date (YYYY-MM-DD), or leave it empty.
upload.error.type: Choose one of the document types, or leave it to the source's.
upload.error.notStarted: Stored, but its ingest did not start
upload.error.notStartedDetail: Temporal did not answer, so the parse did not start. The file is stored: upload the same file again to start its ingest.
upload.error.unreachable: The pipeline could not be reached
upload.error.unreachableDetail: The upload did not reach the pipeline, or its answer did not come back. Open the source's documents to see whether it was stored, then upload again if it was not.
upload.error.stalled: The upload stopped: the file stopped arriving
upload.error.stalledDetail: No part of the file arrived for {seconds} seconds, so the upload was stopped. Nothing was stored: check the connection and upload the file again.
upload.error.unanswered: The pipeline did not answer in time
upload.error.unansweredDetail: The whole file reached the pipeline, but no answer came within {seconds} seconds. Open the source's documents to see whether it was stored, and upload it again if it was not: the same bytes are never stored twice.
pipeline.runs.counts: {listed} listed; of the new ones {stored} stored, {duplicates} duplicates, {failed} failed
adminSources.switches.enabled: Enabled: the schedule crawls it while crawling is on
adminSources.switches.disabled: Disabled: the schedule does not crawl it
adminSources.switches.paused: Paused: the schedule does not crawl it
adminSources.switches.disabledPaused: Disabled and paused: the schedule does not crawl it
adminSources.switches.uploadOnly: Upload-only: it lists nothing and is never crawled
adminSources.crawl.title: Crawling ({flag})
adminSources.crawl.defaultOff: Crawling is off by default: the flag registry declares it off, and the pipeline turns it on only when its own environment sets {variable}. The web server cannot read the pipeline's value; make product, the web stack and CI keep it off, since a crawl reads the live regulator sites.
adminSources.crawl.defaultOn: The flag registry declares crawling on by default; the pipeline reads {variable} in its own environment, which the web server cannot read.
adminSources.crawl.offMeans: While it is off, no source is crawled on its schedule and Fetch now is refused without reading any site; uploads still work.
adminSources.crawl.neverScheduled: The schedule has not crawled any source.
adminSources.crawl.scheduledUnknown: The schedule's latest crawl could not be read: {reason} (correlation id {id}).
adminSources.addNote.title: {title}: not built yet
adminSources.access.adminOnly: Only an admin changes a source
adminSources.access.readOnly: Analysts and reviewers read the source; an admin edits its settings, fetches it and uploads its documents.
adminSources.source.description: Source {key}: its settings, its stored documents and its crawl runs.
adminSources.facts.title: The source
adminSources.reasonHelp: At least {min} characters. The pipeline keeps it word for word in its audit entry, with your name.
adminSources.error.reasonShort: Say why in at least {min} characters.
adminSources.error.name: Give the source a name of 1 to {max} characters.
adminSources.error.cadence: Give the cadence as whole seconds from {min} to {max}.
adminSources.error.parameters: Give the parameters as a JSON object, such as {"listing": "notices"}.
adminSources.error.nothingChanged: Nothing to save: you changed no setting.
adminSources.error.staleForm: The form did not say which settings it showed, so nothing was saved. Reload the page and make your change again.
adminSources.settings.title: Settings
adminSources.settings.intro: Change the name, the cadence, the switches or the parameters. Pausing stops the schedule from crawling the source; a crawl that runs finishes.
adminSources.settings.introUploadOnly: Change the name or the parameters. An upload-only source is never crawled, so its cadence and switches change nothing until it lists documents.
adminSources.settings.name: Name
adminSources.settings.cadenceHelp: Seconds between crawls, from {min} (a minute) to {max} (31 days).
adminSources.settings.enabledLabel: Enabled: the schedule may crawl it
adminSources.settings.pausedLabel: Paused: the schedule leaves it until it is resumed
adminSources.settings.parametersHelp: All of the adapter type's parameters as a JSON object; the pipeline checks them again and refuses what the type does not take.
adminSources.settings.confirmBody: Only the settings you changed are sent. The pipeline records the source before and after, with your reason, in its audit log.
adminSources.settings.meanwhile.name: The name changed meanwhile: it is now "{value}".
adminSources.settings.meanwhile.cadence: The cadence changed meanwhile: it is now {seconds} seconds ({duration}).
adminSources.settings.meanwhile.enabled: The enabled switch changed meanwhile: it is now {value}.
adminSources.settings.meanwhile.paused: The paused switch changed meanwhile: it is now {value}.
adminSources.settings.meanwhile.paramete: The parameters changed meanwhile: they are now {value}.
adminSources.settings.meanwhile.nothingS: Nothing was saved. The form now shows the source as the pipeline holds it: make your change again if it still applies.
adminSources.fetch.title: Fetch now
adminSources.fetch.intro: Starts a crawl of this source at once, a paused one included. The pipeline starts it only while crawling is on ({flag}, set by {variable} in its environment, off by default); while it is off the pipeline refuses, reads no regulator site and records no run.
adminSources.fetch.dialogBody: With crawling on, the pipeline records a crawl run and lists the source's site at once; the source reads Fetching until the crawl ends. With {flag} off, it refuses and nothing is read.
adminSources.fetch.started: Crawl started: run {run}, workflow {workflow}. The source reads Fetching until the crawl ends.
adminSources.refusal.crawlOff: Crawling is off, so nothing was fetched
adminSources.refusal.crawlOffDetail: The pipeline starts no crawl while its flag pipeline.crawl is off (CW_PIPELINE_CRAWL_ENABLED, off by default): no regulator site was read and no run was recorded. Crawling is turned on in the pipeline's environment, not from this page.
adminSources.refusal.crawlRunning: A crawl of this source is running
adminSources.refusal.crawlRunningDetail: Wait for it to end; its run shows in the runs below.
adminSources.refusal.uploadOnlyDetail: It lists nothing, so there is no crawl to start: upload its documents instead.
adminSources.refusal.crawlUnavailable: Temporal did not answer, so the crawl did not start
adminSources.refusal.crawlUnavailableDet: The pipeline closed the run it recorded as failed, with why. Send the fetch again in a moment.
adminSources.refusal.notFound: The pipeline holds no source under this key
adminSources.refusal.notFoundDetail: Open the source again from the list of sources.
adminSources.refusal.invalidField: The adapter type does not take these parameters: see why above.
adminSources.documents.title: Documents
adminSources.documents.caption: Documents of this source, the newest publication first ({count} on this page)
adminSources.documents.emptyTitle: No document stored from this source
adminSources.documents.emptyBody: A crawl stores what the source lists; none has stored a document yet.
adminSources.documents.emptyUploadBody: Documents of an upload-only source arrive by upload; none has been uploaded yet.
adminSources.documents.laterBody: The list ended on the page before.
adminSources.runs.title: Crawl runs
adminSources.runs.caption: This source's latest crawl runs ({count} shown)
adminSources.runs.emptyTitle: No crawl has run for this source
adminSources.runs.emptyBody: A run is recorded when the schedule or an admin starts a crawl, which happens only while crawling is on.
adminSources.runs.emptyUploadBody: An upload-only source is never crawled.
adminSources.upload.title: Upload a document
adminSources.upload.intro: This source lists nothing: its documents arrive by upload. A PDF or an HTML page of at most {limit} MB is stored for good and its ingest parses and classifies it.
adminSources.upload.fileHelp: A PDF or an HTML page, at most {limit} MB.
adminSources.upload.typeHelp: Left as the source's type unless you choose one; a type given here is taken as it is.
adminSources.upload.referenceHelp: Its own reference, such as the Act's name or a notification number.
adminSources.upload.confirmBody: The pipeline stores the file under {source} for good (a stored document is never deleted), records it with your reason in its audit log, and starts its ingest.
adminSources.upload.tooLarge: The file is larger than the pipeline takes ({limit} MB at most).
adminSources.upload.wrongType: Choose a PDF or an HTML page.
adminSources.upload.stored: Stored, and its ingest started: the pipeline parses and classifies it now.
adminSources.upload.duplicate: These bytes were stored before (under {source}): nothing was recorded again, and their ingest ran again.
adminSources.upload.lost: No answer came back, so it is not known whether the file was stored. Try again sends the same file: bytes stored before are not stored twice.
writes.lostBody: It is not known whether the pipeline did it. Try again sends exactly the same request.
adminPipeline.intro: The pipeline's operations for the regulatory team: every source's crawl runs, every stored document with how the pipeline reads it, and the outbox rows the relay gave up on.
adminPipeline.viewIntro.runs: Every source's crawl runs, the latest started first: why each ran (the schedule, an admin's fetch, a backfill of history), what its listing found and how it ended.
adminPipeline.viewIntro.documents: Every source's stored documents, the latest first fetch first, each with the type the pipeline reads it as, its classification (by the detector, a person's triage or a person's type on a retry) and its rule extraction by the current prompt. A document opens on its own page, where an admin retries it.
adminPipeline.viewIntro.outbox: The outbox rows the relay marked dead after eight failed sends (their message is also on the topic's .dlq), the newest dead first. Requeue one once its cause is fixed: the relay sends it again on its next pass.
adminPipeline.access.adminOnly: Only an admin retries, requeues or resolves
adminPipeline.access.readOnly: Analysts and reviewers read the pipeline; an admin requeues a dead row.
adminPipeline.filter.sourceInvalid: A source key is lower-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.
adminPipeline.filter.sourcesUnread: The sources could not be read, so only the one named is offered.
adminPipeline.filter.dateInvalid: Give a date (YYYY-MM-DD), or leave it empty.
adminPipeline.filter.toInvalid: Give a date (YYYY-MM-DD) on or after the first one, or leave it empty.
adminPipeline.filter.datesHelp: A publication date filter leaves undated documents out.
adminPipeline.filter.topicHelp: One topic, such as document.parsed; empty for every topic.
adminPipeline.filter.topicInvalid: A topic is lower-case letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter.
adminPipeline.runs.caption: Crawl runs, the latest started first ({count} on this page)
adminPipeline.documents.caption: Stored documents, the latest first fetch first ({count} on this page)
adminPipeline.classifier.retry: A person's type, given on a retry
adminPipeline.confidence.certain: Certain: the text names the type
adminPipeline.confidence.default: The source's type: the text names none
adminPipeline.confidence.conflict: Conflict: the text names another type than the source publishes
adminPipeline.extraction.unparseable: No candidate: the model gave none, twice
adminPipeline.outbox.caption: Dead outbox rows, the newest dead first ({count} on this page)
adminPipeline.outbox.dialogBody: The row goes back to pending with its attempts reset and is due at once: the relay sends it again on its next pass. Its last error stays until a send succeeds. A row that is no longer dead is left as it stands. The pipeline keeps your reason in its audit log.
adminPipeline.requeue.done: Back to pending: the relay sends this {topic} row again on its next pass. Its last error stays until a send succeeds.
adminPipeline.requeue.notDead: The row was not dead ({status}): nothing changed.
adminPipeline.reasonHelp: At least {min} characters. The pipeline keeps it word for word in its audit entry, with your name.
adminPipeline.error.reasonShort: Say why in at least {min} characters.
adminPipeline.empty.runsBody: A run is recorded when the schedule, an admin's fetch or a backfill starts a crawl. The schedule crawls only while crawling (pipeline.crawl) is on, which it is not by default.
adminPipeline.empty.runsFilteredTitle: No crawl run matches the filter
adminPipeline.empty.documentsBody: A crawl stores what a source lists, and an admin uploads what no site lists.
adminPipeline.empty.outboxBody: The relay has sent every event the pipeline wrote, or is still trying: a row goes dead only after eight failed sends.
adminPipeline.empty.outboxFilteredTitle: No dead row of this topic
adminPipeline.empty.filteredBody: Change the filter, or show every one.
adminPipeline.empty.laterBody: The list ended on the page before.
adminPipeline.refusal.ingestRunning: An ingest of this document is running
adminPipeline.refusal.ingestRunningDetai: Wait for it to end (an earlier retry's, its crawl's, a task resolution's or its rule extraction's), then retry.
adminPipeline.refusal.retryRefused: A triage task holds it, or nothing is left to extract
adminPipeline.refusal.retryInvalid: No rule is extracted from this type
adminPipeline.refusal.retryInvalidDetail: Retry it from parse or classify with that type instead: a press release or a statute is kept for reference.
adminPipeline.refusal.keyReused: This request's key was used for another request
adminPipeline.refusal.keyReusedDetail: The pipeline holds a retry under this form's key with another stage, type or reason. Reload the page, which gives the form a new key, and send the retry again.
adminPipeline.refusal.keyRequired: The retry was sent without its key
adminPipeline.refusal.keyRequiredDetail: Reload the page and send it again: the form carries a key that makes a repeat safe.
adminPipeline.refusal.inFlight: The same request is still being handled
adminPipeline.refusal.inFlightDetail: Wait a moment, then reload the page to see what it recorded.
adminPipeline.refusal.temporal: Temporal did not answer: send the same request again
adminPipeline.refusal.temporalDetail: The pipeline could not start the ingest. What it recorded stays recorded, and nothing was started: send the same request again to start it, and nothing is recorded twice.
adminPipeline.refusal.eventNotFound: The outbox holds no such row
adminPipeline.refusal.eventNotFoundDetai: Reload the dead rows: the id is not one the pipeline's outbox holds.
adminPipeline.refusal.documentNotFound: The pipeline holds no stored document under this id
pipelineDocument.intro: One stored document: its record, how the pipeline reads it, and the retries people asked for.
pipelineDocument.classification.title: Classification
pipelineDocument.classification.none: Not classified yet: the ingest classifies a document after its parse.
pipelineDocument.extraction.title: Rule extraction
pipelineDocument.extraction.none: None by the current prompt: a notification, circular or act amendment is extracted after its classification while the extraction is on.
pipelineDocument.retries.title: Retries
pipelineDocument.retries.caption: Retries of the document, the latest first ({count} in all)
pipelineDocument.retries.emptyBody: An admin's retry runs the stored document's ingest again from a stage; each one is listed here.
pipelineDocument.stage.parseHelp: The stored document's whole ingest again: parse (a document no parser read is parsed again), classify (its classification stands), register while knowledge is on, and extract while the extraction is on.
pipelineDocument.stage.classifyHelp: The same, with the detector reading the document again; a person's decision stands.
pipelineDocument.stage.extractHelp: Only the rule extraction, for a document classified on its way to it whose extraction failed or never started.
pipelineDocument.retry.title: Retry the document
pipelineDocument.retry.intro: Runs the stored document's ingest again from a stage, without a new fetch. The request carries a key, so sending the same one again records nothing twice.
pipelineDocument.retry.typeHelp: A type reclassifies the document first: relevant, of that type, certain, by retry, with your name. It beats the detector, and brings back a document set aside or whose triage was dismissed.
pipelineDocument.retry.typeNotExtracted: No rule is extracted from this type: the pipeline refuses an extraction of it. Retry from parse or classify instead.
pipelineDocument.retry.confirmBody: The pipeline records the attempt with your reason and runs the stored document's ingest again from {stage}, under a workflow of its own.
pipelineDocument.retry.confirmBodyTyped: The pipeline reads the document as a {type} from now on (relevant, certain, by retry, with your name), records the attempt with your reason, and runs its ingest again from {stage}.
pipelineDocument.retry.replayed: This request was recorded before, as attempt {attempt} from {stage}: nothing was recorded twice.
pipelineDocument.retry.reclassified: The document is read as a {type} from now on.
pipelineDocument.retry.readOnly: An admin retries a stored document; analysts and reviewers read it.
pipelineDocument.error.stage: Choose the stage the ingest starts again from.
pipelineDocument.error.type: Choose one of the document types, or keep how it is classified.
pipelineTasks.intro: The work people do on stored documents: a manual parse when no parser reads a document, a triage when its text names another type than its source publishes. Open tasks first, oldest first.
pipelineTasks.readOnly: Analysts and reviewers read the tasks; an admin resolves or dismisses them.
pipelineTasks.facts.closedByPipeline: The pipeline, when a parse succeeded
pipelineTasks.empty.openBody: A manual parse opens when no parser reads a stored document, and a triage when a document's text names another type than its source publishes; both come from the pipeline's ingest.
pipelineTasks.empty.laterBody: The list ended on the page before.
pipelineTasks.transcript.label: The document, typed in
pipelineTasks.transcript.help: Blocks in document order, a blank line between two. A line starting with "# " is a heading; lines starting with "|" are a table (cells between the bars; a second line of bars and dashes makes the first its header); "[page 3]" on its own line gives the page of what follows; any other block is a paragraph, its number first when it has one (1., (2), (a)).
pipelineTasks.transcript.counts: Headings: {headings}; paragraphs: {paragraphs}; tables: {tables}; clauses in all: {clauses}
pipelineTasks.transcript.empty: Type the document in: it has no block yet.
pipelineTasks.transcript.emptyHeading: Block {block}: the heading has no text.
pipelineTasks.transcript.emptyParagraph: Block {block}: the paragraph has no text after its number.
pipelineTasks.transcript.noRows: Block {block}: the table has a header but no row.
pipelineTasks.transcript.emptyRow: Block {block}: row {row} of the table has no text in any cell.
pipelineTasks.transcript.tooManyCells: Block {block}: row {row} has more than {max} cells.
pipelineTasks.transcript.tooManyRows: Block {block}: the table has more than {max} rows.
pipelineTasks.transcript.tooManyClauses: The transcript makes {count} clauses; the rulebook takes at most {max}.
pipelineTasks.triage.relevantHelp: Of the type chosen below; the pipeline registers it as that type.
pipelineTasks.triage.irrelevantHelp: Set aside: nothing is registered or extracted.
pipelineTasks.triage.typeHelp: A notification, circular or act amendment goes on to the rule extraction; a press release or a statute is kept for reference.
pipelineTasks.error.relevance: Say whether it is a regulator's document.
pipelineTasks.resolve.confirmTranscript: The pipeline keeps the transcript (clauses in it: {clauses}), resolves the task with your reason, and starts an ingest that parses the document from it, classifies it and, unless the classification sets it aside or holds it, registers it while knowledge is on. From then on the document is parsed from its transcript.
pipelineTasks.resolve.confirmIrrelevant: The document becomes not a regulatory document (certain, by triage, with your name): it is set aside and nothing is registered or extracted. Nothing starts.
pipelineTasks.resolve.confirmExtract: The document becomes a {type} (certain, by triage, with your name): an ingest registers it while knowledge is on and extracts its rule candidate while the extraction is on.
pipelineTasks.resolve.confirmReference: The document becomes a {type} (certain, by triage, with your name): an ingest registers it while knowledge is on and keeps it for reference; nothing is extracted.
pipelineTasks.resolve.replayed: Resolved: this resolution was recorded before, so nothing was recorded twice; its ingest had started (workflow {workflow}).
pipelineTasks.resolve.setAside: Resolved: the document is set aside as not a regulatory document. Nothing starts.
pipelineTasks.dismiss.dialogManualParse: The task closes without a transcript: the document stays unread by any parser and unregistered. The pipeline keeps your reason in its audit log.
pipelineTasks.dismiss.dialogTriage: The task closes without a decision: the document stays held for triage and unregistered (a retry with a type brings it back). The pipeline keeps your reason in its audit log.
pipelineTasks.dismiss.doneManualParse: Dismissed: the document stays unread by any parser and unregistered.
pipelineTasks.dismiss.doneTriage: Dismissed: the document stays held for triage and unregistered; a retry with a type brings it back.
pipelineTasks.refusal.closedDetail: It was resolved or dismissed: another resolution does not change it. Reload the tasks to see how it was closed.
pipelineTasks.refusal.notFound: The pipeline holds no such task
pipelineTasks.refusal.resolutionInvalid: The resolution does not fit the task
